purpose: prove that components work together across their real boundaries, including failure behavior
entry_criteria: Unit tests for the components pass
A test environment with the real or realistic dependencies exists
Contracts between components are written down
procedure: Identify integration points: databases, queues, internal and external services.
Write tests that exercise each point with real or containerized dependencies and seeded data.
Cover failure behavior: timeouts, retries, duplicate delivery, partial failure, schema mismatch.
Isolate tests so each creates and cleans its own data and can run in any order.
Run in CI with the environment started from scratch; capture logs of failures.
Record contract changes and notify consuming teams.
acceptance_criteria: Each integration point has a success and a failure test
Suite passes from a clean environment
Failures include enough logs to diagnose

validation.command: docker compose -f compose.test.yml up -d --wait && pytest -q tests/integration   # example
validation.expect: exit 0; no skipped tests without owners
environment removed; rerun from scratch gives the same result

failure_modes.mode: Tests pass only on a developer machine
failure_modes.detection: CI run fails on clean environment
failure_modes.response: Fix environment definition; BLOCKED until CI is green

failure_modes.mode: Shared test data causes order dependence

failure_modes.detection: No test exercises the real client
failure_modes.response: Add at least one real-boundary test per integration point

worked_example: ILLUSTRATIVE: An order service and a payment adapter are tested against a containerized payment stub that can return success, decline and timeout. The timeout test shows the order stays pending and is retried once.
